original_value: High-quality updates of road information play an important role in smart city planning, sustainable urban expansion, vehicle management, urban planning, traffic navigation, public health and other fields. However, due to interference from road geometry and texture noise, it is difficult to avoid the decline of automation while accurately extracting roads. Therefore, we propose a high-resolution optical satellite image lane-level road extraction method. First, from the perspective of template matching and considering road characteristics and relevant semantic relations, an adaptive correction model, an MLSOH (multi-scale line segment orientation histogram) descriptor, a sector descriptor, and a multiangle beamlet descriptor are proposed to solve the interference from geometry and texture noise in road template matching and tracking. Second, based on refined lane-level tracking, single-lane and double-lane road-tracking modes are designed to extract single-lane and double-lane roads, respectively. In this paper, Pleiades satellite and GF-2 images are selected to set up different scenarios for urban and rural areas. Experiments are carried out on the phenomena that restrict road extraction, such as tree occlusion, building shadow occlusion, road bending, and road boundary blurring. Compared with other methods, the proposed method not only ensures the accuracy of lane-level road extraction but also greatly improves the automation of road extraction.

result.paraphrase: High-quality road information updates are crucial for smart city planning, sustainable urban growth, vehicle management, urban planning, traffic navigation, public health, and related areas. Yet road geometry and texture noise interfere, making it difficult to maintain automation while extracting roads accurately. To address this, we propose a lane-level road extraction method for high-resolution optical satellite images. First, from the viewpoint of template matching and with road characteristics and semantic relationships in mind, we introduce an adaptive correction model, an MLSOH (multi-scale line segment orientation histogram) descriptor, a sector descriptor, and a multiangle beamlet descriptor to reduce the impact of geometric and texture noise in road template matching and tracking. Second, building on refined lane-level tracking, we design single-lane and double-lane road-tracking modes to extract single-lane and double-lane roads, respectively. This paper uses Pleiades satellite and GF-2 images to create different urban and rural scenarios. Experiments are conducted on issues that hinder road extraction, including tree occlusion, building shadow occlusion, road bending, and blurred road boundaries. Compared with other methods, the proposed method not only maintains the accuracy of lane-level road extraction but also greatly enhances road extraction automation.
